name: Physarum highways

sources.title: Rules for biologically inspired adaptive network design
sources.authors: Tero, Takagi, Saigusa, Ito, Bebber, Fricker, Yumiki, Kobayashi, Nakagaki

sources.title: A mathematical model for adaptive transport network in path finding by true slime mold
Physarum can compute shortest paths
IRLS and slime mold: equivalence and convergence

mechanism: Run the slime-mold tube model on the corner graph with the edge ends as food sources. Tubes with flow thicken, the rest thin out. The thick tubes are the highways. Each edge then takes the cheapest way with link cost L / D^beta.
math: Q_ij = D_ij (p_i - p_j) / L_ij; sum_j Q_ij = +I0 at the source, -I0 at the sink, 0 elsewhere; dD_ij/dt = f(|Q_ij|) - D_ij with f(q) = q^g / (1 + q^g). Large g or small I0 gives a tree near the MST or Steiner tree; small g or large I0 keeps loops.
cost: O(T k E sqrt(V)) for T steps and k Laplacian solves (conjugate gradient) per step. 100 nodes (about 400 corners, 3 000 links, T 150, k 6): 0.3 to 1 s. 1000 nodes: 5 to 20 s on the corner graph, CI only, or under 0.5 s on the hub graph of the sections.
params: keep threshold on D 0.01 to 0.2, default 0.05
screen: Boards case-many-groups, small-clustered and mid-fanout (one seed, 100-node cut for mid-fanout). Against shared-all: keep if B1 >= shared-all + 0.05 and B3 q95 <= shared-all + 0.10 on 2 of 3 boards, with 0 rule violations.

name: Physarum agents on a field

sources.title: Characteristics of pattern formation and evolution in approximations of Physarum transport networks

mechanism: Many particles with three forward sensors walk on a grid. Each turns toward the strongest trail, steps, and drops trail. The trail spreads and fades. Nodes emit attractant. The trail network between the nodes, thinned to a skeleton, gives the shared ways of the far view.
math: Sensors at angles -SA, 0, +SA and distance SO; rotate by RA toward the largest sensed value; move SS; deposit dep; trail T <- decay * mean3x3(T). Typical SA 22.5 or 45 degrees, RA 45 degrees, SO 9 cells.
cost: O(T (A + G)) for T steps, A agents and G cells. A 256 x 256 grid with 10 000 agents and 300 steps: 0.3 to 1 s, nearly independent of n. Skeleton extraction O(G).
screen: Level links of case-dense-groups at the far view. Keep only if Z3 faults are 0 and B1 of the level links rises by 0.10 over levelLinks. Expected to drop: a raster model ignores exact boxes.

name: Loops from changing loads

sources.title: Damage and fluctuations induce loops in optimal transport networks
Fluctuations and redundancy in optimal transport networks

mechanism: Leaf veins form loops because the load moves around. Adapt the conductances to several load cases at once (one per collection or per source group). Loops survive where two heavy loads want different ways, so routes get alternatives and the worst detour drops.
math: Minimize the mean dissipation <sum_e Q_e^2 / C_e> over load cases with sum_e C_e^gamma = K. Fixed point: C_e proportional to <Q_e^2>^(1/(1+gamma)), then rescale to the budget K. gamma < 1 gives loops that grow with the spread of the loads.
cost: Per iteration one Laplacian solve per load case, 20 to 60 iterations. 100 nodes: under 0.5 s. 1000 nodes: 2 to 10 s, CI only, or run on the hub graph.
params: budget K as a share of the full graph 0.05 to 0.5
screen: mid-hubs and case-hub-chain. Against NAT-001 at the same kept length: keep if R6 drops by 10% or more and B1 falls by 0.03 or less.

name: Canalization feeder trees to hubs

sources.title: A model for vein formation in higher plants
The control of the patterned differentiation of vascular tissues
Self-organization of the vascular system in plant leaves: inter-dependent dynamics of auxin flux and carrier proteins

mechanism: In a leaf, every cell makes auxin and the stalk drains it. Channels that carry flux get more conductive, so the flow gathers into veins. In each section, make each member node a source and the hub the sink. The routes to the hub merge into one feeder tree.
math: phi_ij = D_ij (c_i - c_j) / L_ij; sum_j phi_ij = s_i with s_i = 1 for each member and -(members) at the hub; dD_ij/dt = |phi_ij|^mu - r D_ij, mu > 1 gives a tree. One solve per step, as NAT-001 with many sources and one sink.
cost: One small solve per step per section. 100 nodes: about 50 ms. 1000 nodes: 0.5 to 1 s.
screen: Router sections on mid-clustered (100-node and 1000-node seeds) and case-hub-chain. Keep if B1 rises by 0.05 or more over today's sections, with R7 not worse.

name: Active walker trails

sources.title: Modelling the evolution of human trail systems
Active walker model for the formation of human and animal trail systems

mechanism: Route all edges in passes. Each route leaves footprints that make the ground more comfortable, and comfort fades back. In the next pass a link costs less near comfortable ground. Routes gather on shared trails, between a direct way system and a minimal way system.
math: dG/dt = (G0 - G) / T + I (1 - G / Gmax) sum_a delta(r - r_a); V_tr(r) = integral exp(-|r - r'| / sigma) G(r') d2r'; heading e_a = (d_a - r_a + grad V_tr) / norm. kappa = I T / sigma^2: small kappa gives direct ways, large kappa a minimal way system.
cost: P passes times the time of the router shared, plus a blur of the comfort grid per pass. P = 4: about 4 times shared. 100 nodes: about 0.4 s. 1000 nodes: a few seconds, CI only.
screen: Against shared-all on case-many-groups, small-clustered and mid-fanout: the front of B1 against R5 q95, and Z10 after one seeded added edge. Keep if it dominates shared-all on one board and is not dominated on the others.

name: Desire-line room

sources.title: Modelling the evolution of human trail systems

mechanism: People cut across a lawn where the paved way makes a long detour. Draw each edge as its straight desire line, weight it by the detour of its first route, and count the weight that crosses each gap. Open the gaps that the desire lines want, so the routes go straighter.
math: demand(g) = sum_e w_e [the straight line of e crosses gap g or the box next to it], w_e = delta_e - 1 from a first routing (or 1). Feed demand to openGaps in place of the lane count, under an area budget.
cost: O(m times gaps crossed) with the bucket grid, plus one routing pass. 100 nodes: under 10 ms plus the route. 1000 nodes: about 50 ms plus the route.
screen: packedGridBoard and nestedGridBoard. Against roomDemand at the same M1: keep if R5 q95 is 5% lower or better.

name: Ant colony router

sources.title: Ant system: optimization by a colony of cooperating agents
Ant colony system: a cooperative learning approach to the traveling salesman problem
MAX-MIN ant system
Structure and formation of ant transportation networks
sources.authors: Latty, Ramsch, Ito, Nakagaki, Sumpter, Middendorf, Beekman

mechanism: Ants of each collection walk the corner graph from source to target. They pick links by pheromone and length. Short tours drop more pheromone, and pheromone evaporates. With one pheromone per collection, the ants of a collection meet on common ways.
math: p_ij = tau_ij^alpha eta_ij^beta / sum_l tau_il^alpha eta_il^beta, eta_ij = 1 / L_ij; tau <- (1 - rho) tau + sum_k Q / L_k; MAX-MIN clamps tau to [tau_min, tau_max]. Final route: the greedy argmax path of tau^alpha eta^beta.
cost: O(I m a len deg) for I iterations, a ants per edge, path length len and degree deg. 100 nodes (I 30, a 4): about 0.1 s. 1000 nodes: about 2 s.
screen: Against shared on case-many-groups, small-clustered and mid-fanout, 5 seeds. Keep if B1 >= shared + 0.03 with R5 q95 not worse. Expected to tie with shared at a higher cost.

name: Expected ants

sources.title: Ant system: optimization by a colony of cooperating agents

mechanism: Replace the sampled ants by their expected visits. The ant walk from a source is a Markov chain with an absorbing target. One linear solve gives the expected visits of each link. The pheromone update uses these values, so the result needs no seed.
math: P = row-normalized tau^alpha eta^beta, with eta_ij = exp(k cos(angle to target)) / L_ij; visits n solve (I - P_T^T) n = e_source on the transient part; flow_ij = n_i P_ij; tau <- (1 - rho) tau + c flow.
cost: Per iteration one sparse solve per source group, as one step of NAT-001. 100 nodes: 0.1 to 0.3 s. 1000 nodes: 2 to 5 s, CI only.
screen: Against NAT-007 and NAT-001 on the same 3 boards. Keep if B1 is within 0.02 of the better of the two at a lower time, with no seed spread.

name: Two-way lanes

sources.title: Self-organized lane formation and optimized traffic flow in army ants
Social force model for pedestrian dynamics

mechanism: On army-ant trails, outbound ants take the outer lanes and returning ants the middle lane. Walkers in a counterflow form lanes by direction. In each run, sort the lanes by direction first (keep right), then by the bundle order, so edges that go one way stay side by side.
math: Lane key = (direction class relative to the run, then the bundle order). Keep right: lanes along the run direction on its right side. Variant outer: two outer lanes for one direction, the middle for the other.
cost: O(sum over runs of k log k). Negligible at 100 and 1000 nodes.
params: weight against the bundle order 0 to 1, default 1
screen: shared-all on case-many-groups and mid-fanout with directed edges. Keep as a style option if end crossings are within +2% of laneOrder bundle. Keep as a default only if they drop.

name: Termite hubs

sources.title: A model for the emergence of pillars, walls and royal chambers in termite nests
sources.authors: Bonabeau, Theraulaz, Deneubourg, Franks, Rafelsberger, Joly, Blanco

sources.title: A brief history of stigmergy

mechanism: Termites drop material where the scent of fresh material is strong, so deposits grow into evenly spaced pillars. Let each straight edge line drop material on a grid. The scent spreads and fades, the peaks grow and space out. Put the hubs of the sections at the peaks.
math: dP/dt = Phi - k1 P + D_P lap(P) - g div(P grad H); dC/dt = k1 P - k2 C; dH/dt = k2 C - k4 H + D_H lap(H). Simplified: C <- C + k C blur(C) - decay C, then local maxima with suppression radius r.
cost: O(T G) plus O(m len) to drop the material. A 128 x 128 grid and 50 steps: under 50 ms at 100 and 1000 nodes.
screen: sections with hubs at the peaks against today's hubs on mid-hubs and case-hub-chain. Keep if R5 q95 drops by 5% with R7 not worse.

name: Optimal channel networks

sources.title: Minimum energy and fractal structures of drainage networks
sources.authors: Rinaldo, Rodriguez-Iturbe, Rigon, Bras, Ijjasz-Vasquez, Marani

sources.title: Fractal river basins: chance and self-organization
Generation and application of river network analogues for use in ecology and evolution

mechanism: River basins form the spanning tree that makes the total energy small, with a cost that grows slower than the flow. For the edges of one fan, find the tree on the corner graph that makes the sum of flow^gamma times length small. Heavy flows merge into trunks.
math: E = sum_i k_i Q_i^gamma L_i with gamma = 0.5; Q_i = edges whose path uses link i. Local move: change the downstream link of one vertex; accept if E drops (or by annealing). Start from the shortest-path tree.
cost: Sweeps S times V times degree times depth. 100 nodes (400 corners, S 20): under 50 ms per fan. 1000 nodes: about the time of trunks times 2.
params: annealing T0 0 (greedy) to 1, with a seed
screen: trunks against this tree on mid-fanout and small-clustered. Keep if its (B1, B3 q95) point is on the front against the trunks rule at each split.

name: Branched transport junctions

sources.title: Minimum cost communication networks
Optimal paths related to transport problems
Optimal transportation networks: models and theory

mechanism: The cost of a way grows with its load as w^alpha with alpha below 1, so sharing pays. For each fan, merge targets into Y junctions where the weighted pulls of the three branches balance. alpha 1 gives straight edges, alpha 0 a Steiner tree. The junction angle follows the load.
math: cost = sum_e w_e^alpha L_e. At a Y: w0^alpha e0 + w1^alpha e1 + w2^alpha e2 = 0 (unit vectors out of the junction), so cos(theta1) = (w0^(2 alpha) + w1^(2 alpha) - w2^(2 alpha)) / (2 w0^alpha w1^alpha). Equal split: cos(theta/2) = 2^(alpha - 1): 120, 90 and 74.9 degrees at alpha 0, 0.5 and 2/3. Junction point by weighted Weiszfeld steps.
cost: O(k^2) per fan for the merge order plus O(k iterations) for the junctions. Under 10 ms at 100 nodes, under 100 ms at 1000 nodes, plus A* repair of branches that hit a box.
screen: trunks with these junctions against split on mid-fanout and small-clustered. Keep if B6 max <= 60 degrees and B1 >= trunks, with 0 rule violations after the repair.

name: Murray widths and angles

sources.title: The physiological principle of minimum work: I. The vascular system and the cost of blood volume
Optimality principles in arterial branching
On connecting large vessels to small: the meaning of Murray's law

mechanism: Vessels keep the cube of the radius constant over a split. Give each closed bundle and each level link a drawn width that grows as count^(1/3), not as the count. Thick bundles stay narrow, merges look continuous, and the gaps need less room. Use the matching junction angle.
math: r0^3 = sum_i r_i^3, so width = w0 k^(1/3). Minimum-volume angle: cos(theta1) = (r0^4 + r1^4 - r2^4) / (2 r0^2 r1^2). With r^3 proportional to the flow, this is NAT-012 with alpha = 2/3.
cost: O(segments). Negligible.
screen: shared-all on case-many-groups: room demand with widths k^(1/3) against lane widths k. Keep if M1 drops by 5% or more with M4 = 0.

name: Vascular tree by constrained construction

sources.title: Computer-optimization of vascular trees
A three-dimensional model for arterial tree representation, generated by constrained constructive optimization

mechanism: Grow the tree of a fan one target at a time. Join each new target to the existing segment where a new split adds the least total volume, with radii from Murray's law. Then scale the radii of the whole tree again.
math: Volume V = pi sum_i r_i^2 L_i; resistance R = 8 eta L / (pi r^4); flows fixed by the targets; r from Murray's law with exponent 3. For each candidate segment, place the split point by weighted Weiszfeld steps and keep the least dV.
cost: O(k^2) candidates per fan, O(k^3) worst case with rescaling. k up to 50: a few ms per fan at 100 and 1000 nodes.
screen: Same boards as NAT-012. Keep if B1 is higher than NAT-012 at an equal B3 q95. Otherwise merge it into NAT-012 as its construction order.

name: Space colonization trunks

sources.title: Modeling and visualization of leaf venation patterns
sources.authors: Runions, Fuhrer, Lane, Federl, Rolland-Lagan, Prusinkiewicz

sources.title: Modeling trees with a space colonization algorithm

mechanism: The targets of a fan are attractors. From the source plug the tree grows in steps. Each attractor pulls its nearest tree node. Each pulled node grows a new node along the mean direction to its attractors. An attractor dies when a node comes within the kill distance.
math: n_v = sum over s in S(v) of (s - v) / |s - v|; v' = v + D n_v / |n_v|; remove s when |s - v| < d_k; S(v) holds the attractors within d_i whose nearest node is v.
cost: O(steps (S + V) log) with the bucket grid. A fan needs span / D steps. Under 10 ms at 100 nodes, under 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
screen: mid-fanout and small-clustered against trunks. Keep if B1 rises by 0.05 with B3 q95 within +0.10 and 0 rule violations.

name: Closed venation backbone for levels

sources.title: Modeling and visualization of leaf venation patterns
sources.authors: Runions, Fuhrer, Lane, Federl, Rolland-Lagan, Prusinkiewicz

sources.title: The relative neighbourhood graph of a finite planar set

mechanism: In closed venation, a vein grows to a source from each node in its relative neighbourhood, which makes loops. At a zoom level, link the items by their relative neighbourhood graph and route each level link along it, so the far view shows a calm network with a few loops.
math: Relative neighbourhood graph: p-q is a link if no r has max(d(p, r), d(q, r)) < d(p, q). Each level link takes the cheapest way on that graph with cost L (1 - discount if shared).
cost: O(k log k) through the Delaunay graph, or O(k^2) for k items. Under 10 ms for up to 1000 items.
screen: Level links of case-dense-groups and case-many-groups. Keep if the level faults (Z3) are not worse and the ink of the level drops by 10%.

name: Balancing-factor trees

sources.title: One rule to grow them all: a general theory of neuronal branching and its practical application

mechanism: Dendrites follow one rule: grow a minimum spanning tree where each new point joins the tree at the place that makes its wire length plus bf times its path length to the root least. bf 0 gives the least wire, a large bf gives direct paths. One knob trades ink against detour.
math: Greedy (Prim with a changed cost): add t* = argmin over t not in T, v in T of d(t, v) + bf PL(v), with PL(v) the path length from the root to v. Joining at segments (not only nodes) adds Steiner points.
cost: O(k^2) per fan, or O(k) A* searches with corner-graph distances. Under 10 ms at 100 nodes, under 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
screen: Sweep bf over 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.7 and 1 on mid-fanout and small-clustered. Keep if one bf dominates the default point of trunks on (B1, B3 q95).

result.note: The option `fan: tree` of `trunks` is off by default. bf 0.2 and 0.4 beat `trunks` on B1 and the B3 q95 on dense-groups (B1 0.081 to 0.095 with bf 0.2). On small-clustered, the q95 falls but B1 falls 4%. hub-chain and many-groups do not change. A smaller bf gives more B1, so a screen of bf 0 and 0.1 is next.

name: Knee of the plant Pareto front

sources.title: High-resolution laser scanning reveals plant architectures that reflect universal network design principles

mechanism: Plant shoots sit on the Pareto front of total length against the path length to the root, at a place that depends on their conditions. Compute the front of each fan by a sweep of the weight, and give each fan its own knee point, not one global knob.
math: cost_a(T) = a L(T) + (1 - a) sum_t PL(t); front by a in {0, 0.1, ..., 1} with the greedy tree of NAT-017; knee = the point farthest from the chord of the normalized front.
cost: 11 times NAT-017. Under 0.1 s at 100 nodes, under 1 s at 1000 nodes.
screen: Against NAT-017 with its best fixed bf: keep if the hypervolume of (B1, B3) is higher on 2 of 3 boards.

name: Bronchial space-filling splits

sources.title: A three-dimensional model of the human airway tree
An optimal bronchial tree may be dangerous

mechanism: The airway tree splits its region in two, gives each child the flow of its half, and points each child toward the center of its half. For a trunk, split the targets in two by a line through the tip, branch toward the center of each half, and repeat until one target is left.
math: Flow ratio r = Q1 / Q0. Child direction: toward the centroid of its subset. Angles from r with Murray's exponent: cos(theta1) = (1 + r^(4/3) - (1 - r)^(4/3)) / (2 r^(2/3)). Branch length: a share of the distance to the centroid.
cost: O(k log^2 k) per fan. Under 10 ms at 100 and 1000 nodes.
params: split: count | weight | widest angle gap
screen: Same boards as NAT-017. Keep if not dominated by the best bf of NAT-017 on (B1, B3 q95) and B6 is lower.

name: Mycelial spanner backbone

sources.title: Biological solutions to transport network design
On sparse spanners of weighted graphs
Rules for biologically inspired adaptive network design

mechanism: Fungi build a cheap tree and then fuse hyphae to add loops where transport is slow. Build a minimum spanning tree over the hubs as the backbone. Add a shortcut between two hubs when the backbone way is more than t times their direct distance and much traffic goes between them.
math: Greedy t-spanner over the hubs: for pairs in order of decreasing demand (ties by distance), add (u, v) if d_B(u, v) > t d(u, v) and w_uv >= w_min. Report the measures of Tero 2010: length over MST, mean distance over MST, and the fault tolerance.
cost: O(h^2 log h) for h hubs. h is about n / 8: under 1 ms at 100 nodes, about 10 ms at 1000 nodes.
screen: sections on case-hub-chain and mid-hubs. Keep if R6 drops by 10% with B1 lower by 0.02 at most.

name: Tropism growth router

sources.title: A dynamic root system growth model based on L-Systems
A fast marching level set method for monotonically advancing fronts

mechanism: A root tip grows in steps and turns toward a cue with a limited turn rate, and away from stones. Grow each route from its plug along the normal. Turn toward the falling geodesic distance to the target, at most a set angle per step, and away from near boxes. The path has bounded curvature.
math: h_(k+1) = normalize(h_k + s_t grad(phi_target) + s_o grad(phi_obstacle)), turn per step <= dtheta_max, step length s. phi_target is the geodesic distance field (no local minima). Curvature <= dtheta_max / s.
cost: One distance field per target, cached: O(G log G) each. 100 nodes with a 128 x 128 grid: 0.3 to 1 s. 1000 nodes: CI only, or guide by the A* path of corners in place of a field.
params: max turn 5 to 45 degrees per step, default 15
screen: case-many-groups and small-clustered against corners with the clothoid curve. Keep if C3 median is lower, R5 q95 is within +5% and no rule fails.

name: Axon zipper

sources.title: Axon tension regulates fasciculation/defasciculation through the control of axon shaft zippering
Models of axon guidance and bundling during development
A model of fasciculation and sorting in mixed populations of axons

mechanism: Axons that touch at a small angle zip together: adhesion pulls them into one bundle and tension resists. After any router, find pairs of legs that run near and almost parallel. Zip them onto one shared line when the shared length gain beats the cost of extra length and turn.
math: Zip if a overlap - tension dL > 0, with angle <= theta_max and distance <= d_max. Zipped line: length-weighted mean of the two legs. Our reading of the zipper vertex balance: cos(theta/2) = 1 - Gamma / (2 T), adhesion Gamma, tension T.
cost: O(S log S) for the pairs with the bucket grid, a few passes. About 5 ms at 100 nodes, 50 to 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
params: adhesion ratio Gamma / T 0 to 1, default 0.3
screen: A post step on corners and on plugs routes, case-dense-groups and small-clustered. Keep if B1 rises by 0.05, B4 rises by 0.03 at most and R9 stays 0.

name: Harmonic field router

sources.title: Path planning using Laplace's equation
Real-time obstacle avoidance for manipulators and mobile robots
Mathematical guidance for axons

mechanism: Growth cones climb an attractant from the target and turn from repellents. Solve Laplace's equation in the free space with the target low and the boxes as walls, then follow the gradient. A harmonic field has no local minimum, so each route arrives. With a source and a sink, the routes are electric field lines.
math: lap(phi) = 0 in the free space; phi = 0 on the target; boxes Dirichlet (phi = 1) or Neumann (d phi / dn = 0, insulating). Route: dx/ds = -grad(phi) / |grad(phi)|. Dipole: +1 at the source, -1 at the target.
cost: One solve per target: O(G iterations) by SOR or multigrid. A 128 x 128 grid and 200 iterations: 3 million updates per target. 100 nodes: 0.3 to 1 s. 1000 nodes: CI only, or only for the level links.
screen: Level links of case-dense-groups and case-many-groups. Keep if Z3 faults are 0 and R8 rises by 20% over levelLinks.

name: Pioneer and follower order

sources.title: Models of axon guidance and bundling during development

mechanism: Pioneer axons grow first and later axons follow them. In the routers with shared ways, the order of the edges decides which ways become shared. Route the pioneers first: the edges with the longest span, or with the most edges between their two sections. The followers then get the discount.
math: Order key = -span(e), or -load(e) with load the number of edges between the same two sections, ties by edge id. Then the router shared runs as today.
cost: O(m log m) on top of shared. No change in time class.
screen: shared-all with the 4 orders on 5 boards, 5 seeds each. Keep an order if A12 >= 0.64 on B1 against the input order, with R5 q95 not worse.

result.note: The default order `span` (the longest first) is the pioneer order. The base is `order: input`. With `shared-all`, B1 rises 6.2% and 5.3% on small-clustered and dense-groups, and R1 falls 19% and 10%. With `shared`, B1 rises 6.2% on dense-groups and R1 falls 0.7%. On many-groups with `shared-all`, R1 rises 7%. The order `load` does not beat `span`.

name: Soap-film Steiner trees

sources.title: How to find Steiner minimal trees in Euclidean d-space
A new class of Steiner tree heuristics with good performance: the iterated 1-Steiner approach
Obstacle-avoiding Euclidean Steiner trees in the plane: an exact algorithm

mechanism: A soap film between pins makes the shortest network, with three ways at 120 degrees at each junction. For each fan or collection with three ends or more, build a Steiner tree that avoids the boxes, and route the edges along it. It is the upper bound of ink saving.
math: Minimize sum L. Steiner points have degree 3 and angles of 120 degrees. Iterated 1-Steiner: add the candidate point that cuts the MST length most, repeat. Rectilinear: candidates on the Hanan grid.
cost: Iterated 1-Steiner: O(k^3 log k) per fan, k up to 30: a few ms. Exact methods only for small fans. Plus A* repair near boxes.
screen: mid-fanout and small-clustered: B1 against NAT-012 at alpha 0. Keep as the reference bound of B1 in the bench, not as a default.

name: Elastic band curves

sources.title: Elastic bands: connecting path planning and control
The heat equation shrinking convex plane curves

mechanism: A soap film in two dimensions is a shortest line, and a rubber band tightens until it touches its pegs. Treat each route as an elastic band. Tension shortens and smooths it, and a soft push from the boxes keeps clearance. Run a fixed number of steps.
math: x_i <- x_i + k_c (x_(i-1) + x_(i+1) - 2 x_i) + k_r sum_b grad(rho_b(x_i)), rho_b = max(0, d0 - dist(x, b)). Curve-shortening flow: dx/dt = kappa N.
cost: O(P iterations) with the bucket grid. About 10 ms at 100 nodes, about 100 ms at 1000 nodes.
screen: The curve step on corners routes, case-many-groups and small-clustered. Keep if C3 median drops by 20% against smooth, with the counts curve-clear and curve-ends at 0.

name: Crystal metric

sources.title: Geometric models of crystal growth
Zur Frage der Geschwindigkeit des Wachsthums und der Auflosung der Krystallflachen

mechanism: Crystals grow fastest along preferred directions, so they take polygon shapes. Route under a metric whose unit ball is a polygon: a square for an orthogonal style, an octagon for an octilinear style, a circle for free style. Routes then use few directions and few bends.
math: ||v||_W = min { lambda : v in lambda W } for the Wulff shape W, plus a bend cost b per turn. Shortest path on a state graph of (corner, direction).
cost: A* on the corner graph times 4 or 8 directions: 4 to 8 times corners. 100 nodes: about 0.2 s. 1000 nodes: 2 to 5 s.
screen: corners with the octagon against corners on small-clustered and grid-400. Keep if R3 drops by 20% with R5 q95 within +5%.

name: Lightning growth

sources.title: Fractal dimension of dielectric breakdown
Diffusion-limited aggregation, a kinetic critical phenomenon
Fast animation of lightning using an adaptive mesh

mechanism: Lightning and diffusion-limited aggregation grow a branched channel in a Laplacian field. The growth chance of each frontier cell is the field there to the power eta. eta 1 is aggregation, a large eta gives straight channels. A channel grown from a source toward its targets is a branched trunk.
math: lap(phi) = 0, phi = 0 on the channel, phi = 1 at the targets; p_i = |grad(phi_i)|^eta / sum_j |grad(phi_j)|^eta. Deterministic limit: grow at the argmax.
cost: One Laplace solve per growth step: 1 000 steps on 10 000 cells with 50 iterations is 500 million updates, seconds per fan. CI only.
screen: One fan of mid-fanout at 100 nodes. Keep only if B1 >= NAT-015 and R4 <= NAT-015. Expected to drop.

name: Crack partition

sources.title: Hierarchical crack pattern as formed by successive domain divisions
Four sided domains in hierarchical space dividing patterns

mechanism: Drying mud cracks in order. Each new crack splits one domain across its long side and meets the older cracks at right angles, so the domains nest. Split each section by a crack that follows the gaps between the boxes, not a straight line, and pick the crack that cuts the fewest edges.
math: Crack = cheapest path across the cell on the gap graph (the dual of the free space), cost = edges cut + lambda length; across the longer side; ends at the older crack (T junction). Balance limit beta as the rule cut.
cost: One shortest path on the gap graph per split. 100 nodes: a few ms. 1000 nodes: about 50 ms.
params: most turns of a crack 0 to 8
screen: Against cut on the 10 boards of GRP-R at the same k. Keep if G2 at the far view is lower on 6 of 10 and G5 is not worse.

name: Erosion of a cost field

sources.title: A detachment-limited model of drainage basin evolution
The synthesis and rendering of eroded fractal terrains

mechanism: Water carves valleys where flow gathers, and slopes creep smooth. Route all edges on a cost grid, count the routes per cell as the flow, lower the cost there, smooth the field, and route again. Channels form, and the smoothing sets their spacing.
math: dz/dt = U - K A^m S^n + D lap(z), with z the cost field, A the route count per cell and S the local slope. A larger D / K gives wider spacing between channels.
cost: P passes of grid A* for m edges plus a blur. 100 nodes, 128 x 128 grid: about 0.1 s per pass. 1000 nodes: CI only.
screen: Against NAT-005 on the same boards. Keep if not dominated on (B1, R5 q95). Otherwise make it an option of NAT-005.

name: Ripple spacing of plugs

sources.title: Eolian dunes: computer simulations and attractor interpretation
A theoretical model for aeolian impact ripples

mechanism: Sand ripples settle at an even spacing through a short-range push. On each side of a box, treat the plugs as beads: each is pulled toward the place that faces its other end and pushed from its neighbours. Keep the order of the targets. The exact answer is an isotonic fit with a gap.
math: Minimize sum_i (x_i - t_i)^2 subject to x_(i+1) - x_i >= s and the side limits, with the plugs in the order of their target angles. Substitute y_i = x_i - i s and run pool-adjacent-violators: exact, O(k).
cost: O(k log k) per side for the sort. Negligible at 100 and 1000 nodes.
screen: small-clustered and mid-hubs. Keep if R11 q05 rises by 0.2 with R1 not worse. Fixed plugs do not move.

result.note: This rider of WILD-002 is the option `plugGap: 8`. The R11 q05 rises by more than 0.2, but R1 grows 3% to 5% on dense-groups and small-clustered.

name: Phyllotaxis plug slots

sources.title: A better way to construct the sunflower head

mechanism: Sunflower seeds sit at golden-angle steps, so each new seed lands in the largest gap and no seed moves. Give the plug slots of a hub or a round item golden-angle steps, or golden-ratio steps along a side. A new edge adds one slot and moves no other plug.
math: theta_k = k 137.508 degrees; along a side, x_k = frac(k / phi) times the side length (a Weyl sequence). The ratio of the smallest to the largest gap stays above 1 / phi. Edges take slots by sorted angle.
cost: O(k log k) per side. Negligible.
screen: small-clustered and case-hub-chain, one seeded added edge. Keep if the moved share of Z10 drops by 30% with R11 q05 >= 0.35.

name: Foam groups

sources.title: Least squares quantization in PCM
Capacity-constrained point distributions: a variant of Lloyd's method
The physics of foams

mechanism: A dry foam relaxes to cells of equal area with walls that meet at 120 degrees. Start with k seeds, give each node to a seed with a capacity, move each seed to the center of its nodes, and repeat. Groups get equal sizes and round shapes. Repeat inside each group for the next level.
math: Capacity-constrained Voronoi: swap pairs of nodes between two groups when the swap lowers sum |c_v - s_g|^2 and keeps |g| = n / k. Lloyd step: s_g <- mean of c_v in g. Optional edge term alpha cut(g).
cost: O(t n log n) with the swaps. Under 10 ms at 1000 nodes for k 4 to 16.
screen: Against kd on the 10 boards of GRP-R at the same k. Keep if G4 rises by 0.05 and G5 is not worse.

name: Grassfire corridors

sources.title: A transformation for extracting new descriptors of shape
Voronoi diagrams: a survey of a fundamental geometric data structure

mechanism: A grass fire lit at all box edges burns inward. The fronts meet on the medial axis, the line farthest from all boxes. Use the medial axis of the free space as the road graph. Highways then run down the middle of the gaps with the most clearance, and short spurs join the plugs.
math: Medial axis = the Voronoi diagram of the box sides (or a grid distance transform and its ridges). Link cost L (1 + lambda / clearance). Spurs: the shortest clear segment from a plug to the axis.
cost: O(n log n) for the segment Voronoi diagram, or O(G) on a grid. About 50 ms at 1000 nodes, then routing as shared.
screen: shared-all on the axis graph against shared-all on the corner graph, small-clustered and case-dense-groups. Keep if tight drops by 50% with R5 q95 within +10%.

name: Snell merges

sources.title: Fermat's principle of least time (refraction, Snell's law)

mechanism: Light bends where it enters a faster medium. If a highway costs d < 1 per unit, the cheapest way to join it arrives at the angle acos(d) to the highway, not at a right angle. Put each merge and exit point where the route meets the highway at that angle.
math: Minimize sqrt(h^2 + x^2) + d (X - x): the optimum has cos(theta) = d. The merge point lies h d / sqrt(1 - d^2) before the foot of the perpendicular. Scratch check: d 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 give 75.5, 60.0, 41.4 degrees.
cost: O(1) per merge and exit. Negligible.
params: discount d 0.3 to 0.9 (the discount of shared)
fallback: perpendicular when the line is not clear
screen: shared and trunks on case-many-groups and mid-fanout. Needs B6 in the suite. Keep if B6 max <= 75 degrees and R9 stays 0.

result.note: The option `merge: snell` of `shared` is off by default. The B6 max falls on each board with merges: 8% to 27%. The ink rises 0.5% at most. The crossings rise 6% to 13% (18 to 24 on hub-chain), because the new merge lines cut across other routes. The option is only in `shared`, not in `trunks`.

name: Magnetic flow direction

sources.title: Graph drawing by the magnetic spring model

mechanism: In the magnetic spring model, edges act as compass needles that turn to a field: parallel, radial or round. Add a cost to each leg that points against a chosen field. All routes then flow one way, for example left to right or out from the center, and fewer routes go back.
math: Sugiyama and Misue: torque proportional to c_m b |d|^a theta^b. Here, leg cost = L (1 + c_m ((1 - cos theta) / 2)^beta), theta the angle between the leg and the field at its midpoint.
cost: The time of corners or shared plus O(1) per link. No change in time class.
screen: mid-fanout with a parallel field along the flow. Keep if R7 drops by 30% with R5 q95 within +5% against corners.

name: Current corridors

sources.title: A measure of betweenness centrality based on random walks
Centrality measures based on current flow
Graph sparsification by effective resistances

mechanism: Put one unit of current in at each source and take it out at its target. The current spreads over all ways, more on the short ones. Add the absolute currents of all edges on each link of the corner graph. Links with a high total are the corridors for highways. The other edges route alone.
math: L p = b_e for each edge (or each source group); I_link = sum_e |c_ij (p_i - p_j)|; a corridor is a link with I >= the q quantile. Then shared with the discount on corridor links. Faster: a seeded sketch with O(log m) random +1/-1 right sides.
cost: One Laplacian solve per source group. 100 nodes: about 0.1 s. 1000 nodes: 1 to 3 s, or under 0.5 s with a sketch of 16 solves.
screen: Against shared-all on case-many-groups, small-clustered and mid-fanout. Keep if not dominated on (B1, B3 q95) and B4 is lower.

name: Boids lanes

sources.title: Flocks, herds and schools: a distributed behavioral model
Novel type of phase transition in a system of self-driven particles

mechanism: Sample each route into points. Each point steers by three rules among the near points of other routes with a similar direction: align with them, move toward them, and keep a minimum distance. Bundles form with lanes at the separation distance, not on one line.
math: dx_i = w_a (mean u_j - u_i) + w_c (mean x_j - x_i) + w_s sum (x_i - x_j) / |x_i - x_j|^2 over |x_i - x_j| < s; neighbours within r with cos(direction) >= c; a spring to the first route and a push from the boxes.
cost: O(iterations P neighbours). 100 nodes (4 000 points, 30 iterations): a few ms. 1000 nodes: about 0.3 s.
screen: A post step on corners routes, small-clustered and case-dense-groups. Keep if B7 drops by 10% with R9 at 0.

name: Cell-sorting groups

sources.title: Reconstruction of tissues by dissociated cells
Simulation of biological cell sorting using a two-dimensional extended Potts model

mechanism: Mixed cells sort out because like cells stick more strongly. Give each node a group label. On the graph of neighbours on the board, a label pays an adhesion cost for each neighbour with another label and gains for each edge kept inside. A size term keeps groups near the target size.
math: H = sum over neighbour pairs of J (1 - delta(s_i, s_j)) - sum over edges of w delta(s_i, s_j) + lambda sum_g (a_g - A)^2. Zero-temperature sweeps: each node takes the neighbour label with the least H.
cost: O(sweeps (n kappa + m)): about 5 ms per sweep at 1000 nodes, 20 sweeps.
screen: Against cut on the 10 boards of GRP-R at the same k. Keep if G2 at the far view is lower on 6 of 10 with G5 not worse.

name: Reaction-diffusion hub spacing

sources.title: The chemical basis of morphogenesis
A theory of biological pattern formation

mechanism: An activator that excites itself and a fast inhibitor make spots at an even spacing. Seed the activator with the node density on a coarse grid and run it. The spots are the hub places, spaced by the range of the inhibitor. Nodes join the nearest spot. A larger range gives the next level.
math: da/dt = rho a^2 / h - mu_a a + D_a lap(a) + rho_0 s(x); dh/dt = rho a^2 - mu_h h + D_h lap(h). The spacing grows with sqrt(D_h / D_a).
cost: O(T G): a 128 x 128 grid and 2 000 steps, 0.1 to 0.3 s, nearly independent of n.
screen: Hubs from the spots against the hubs of the quadtree in sections. Keep if the spread of log(Z5) drops by 30% with G2 worse by 0.03 at most.

name: Meinhardt nets

sources.title: Morphogenesis of lines and nets

mechanism: Meinhardt showed that an activator and inhibitor with a substrate that the new cells use up make net lines that branch toward the places in need, like veins. Make the edge ends the places in need. The line cells that remain are a highway net.
math: da/dt = c s a^2 / h - mu a + D_a lap(a) + rho_0 y; dh/dt = c s a^2 - nu h + D_h lap(h); ds/dt = c_0 - gamma s - eps y s + D_s lap(s); dy/dt = d a - e y + y^2 / (1 + f y^2). y marks the line cells and does not go back.
cost: O(T G) with 4 fields: a 256 x 256 grid and 5 000 steps is more than 1 billion updates, seconds. CI only.
screen: small-clustered at the far view only. Drop unless B1 >= NAT-001 at a lower time. Expected to drop.

name: Remodelling room

sources.title: Adaptive bone-remodeling theory applied to prosthetic-design analysis
sources.authors: Huiskes, Weinans, Grootenboer, Dalstra, Fudala, Slooff

mechanism: Bone adds mass where the load is high and removes it where the load is low. Give the gaps a fixed extra area. In each pass, a gap grows by its lane load over its width and shrinks where the load is low. Then route again.
math: Stimulus S_g = lanes_g laneWidth / w_g; w_g <- w_g (1 + eta (S_g / S* - 1)); rescale so that sum w_g = budget. Huiskes: d rho / dt = B (S / rho - k).
cost: P passes of route plus roomDemand. 100 nodes with P = 3: about 0.3 s. 1000 nodes: a few seconds.
screen: packedGridBoard: M4 at M1 1.25 against roomDemand with maxGrowth 0.25 (ROOM-A: 2 lane routes through a box at 1.46). Keep if M4 is 0 at M1 1.35 or less.

name: Annealing of the discrete choices

sources.title: Optimization by simulated annealing
Drawing graphs nicely using simulated annealing

mechanism: Cooling metal finds a low-energy state because it accepts some worse moves while it is hot. Search the discrete choices that the greedy steps fix: the side of each free plug, the lane order of each run and which edges join a bundle. The energy is a weighted sum of the MEAS0 scores.
math: Accept a move with probability min(1, exp(-dE / T)); T_(k+1) = c T_k; E = sum_i w_i score_i, each score scaled as in the method of MEAS0.
cost: Moves times the time of dE. Lane orders only (local crossings): about 0.1 s for 10 000 moves. With a reroute per move: seconds to minutes, CI only.
screen: Lane order only, shared-all on case-many-groups. Keep if end crossings drop by 10% against laneOrder bundle.

name: Evolution of the options (NSGA-II)

sources.title: Adaptation in natural and artificial systems
A fast and elitist multiobjective genetic algorithm: NSGA-II

mechanism: A population of option settings evolves by crossover and mutation. Sorting by Pareto rank and crowding keeps a spread-out front of the measures. It gives TUNE a front over many options at once, not one sweep per option.
math: Fast non-dominated sort O(M N^2), crowding distance, binary tournament, simulated binary crossover and polynomial mutation.
cost: Generations times population times one route: 50 x 40 x 0.1 s = 200 s at 100 nodes. CI only.
screen: Two options of shared (discount, margin) against the grid sweep of OPTS. Keep if the front has the same hypervolume within 2% with fewer runs.

name: MAP-Elites atlas of settings

sources.title: Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites

mechanism: Quality-diversity search keeps the best setting in each cell of a grid of looks, for example ink saved against detour. The result is an atlas of distinct good settings. The playground shows it, so a reader picks a look and not a weight.
math: Archive A[cell(b(x))] keeps argmax f. Loop: pick an elite with a seeded draw, mutate it, evaluate it, and insert it if it beats the elite of its cell.
cost: As NAT-044: CI only for a full atlas. A precomputed atlas per example board is a static file.
params: descriptors: B1 x R5 | B2 x C3
screen: shared with the highway curve on one board. Keep if the archive fills 30% more cells than a grid sweep with the same number of runs.

name: Particle swarm and CMA-ES tuning

sources.title: Particle swarm optimization
Completely derandomized self-adaptation in evolution strategies

mechanism: Particles fly through the space of options, pulled to their own best and to the best of the swarm. CMA-ES moves and shapes a Gaussian cloud. Both tune the continuous options for one weighted score with few runs.
math: PSO: v <- w v + c1 r1 (p - x) + c2 r2 (g - x); x <- x + v. CMA-ES: sample N(m, sigma^2 C), then update m, C and sigma from the ranks.
cost: 20 particles x 30 iterations x one route. CI only above 100 nodes.
screen: Two options of shared against the grid sweep. Keep if it reaches 1% of the best grid score with a third of the runs or fewer.

name: Firefly and bee searches

sources.title: Firefly algorithms for multimodal optimization
A powerful and efficient algorithm for numerical function optimization: artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm
The bees algorithm
sources.authors: Pham, Ghanbarzadeh, Koc, Otri, Rahim, Zaidi

sources.title: Metaheuristics: the metaphor exposed

mechanism: Fireflies move toward brighter ones with an attraction that fades with distance, so the swarm splits over several peaks. A bee colony sends more bees to rich sites and scouts to new ones. Both find several distinct good settings. They are close cousins of particle swarms.
math: Firefly: x_i <- x_i + beta0 exp(-gamma r_ij^2) (x_j - x_i) + alpha (rand - 0.5). ABC: v_ij = x_ij + phi (x_ij - x_kj), phi in [-1, 1]; onlookers pick i with p_i = fit_i / sum fit; a scout replaces a site after limit failures.
cost: As NAT-046.
screen: As NAT-046. Keep only if it finds a second distinct optimum that NAT-046 misses (hypervolume +5%). Expected to drop.

name: Use-it-or-lose-it pruning

sources.title: Decreasing-rate pruning optimizes the construction of efficient and robust distributed networks

mechanism: The brain makes too many synapses and then prunes the ones that carry little traffic, at a rate that falls with time. Start from all the runs of shared-all. Prune the runs that save the least, at a falling rate, and route the edges of a pruned run alone.
math: Prune share p_t = p0 r^t; usage u = (edges of the run - 1) times its length; remove the lowest u first. Navlakha and others: a falling rate gives more efficient and robust networks than a constant or a rising rate.
cost: Rounds times the reroute of the affected edges: 2 to 3 times shared-all.
screen: shared-all on case-many-groups and mid-fanout. Keep if B4 drops by 0.05 with B1 lower by 0.03 at most.

name: Multiscale Physarum across levels

sources.title: Rules for biologically inspired adaptive network design

mechanism: Run the tube model on the coarse level first, on the items and their links. Use its tubes as the starting conductance of the next finer level. The highways of the fine level then follow the level links of the far view, so a zoom keeps the map.
math: D^(d+1)_0(link) = 1 + kappa D^(d)(the corridor of its parent items), then NAT-001 at level d+1 with fewer steps.
cost: The sum over the levels, with fewer steps at the fine levels: about half of NAT-001.
screen: nestedGridBoard and case-dense-groups against NAT-001 alone. Needs Z9 in the suite. Keep if Z9 drops by 30%.
